title: USMLE Step 3
description: Final USMLE licensing exam taken during residency. Two-day exam testing biomedical + clinical sciences applied to patient management + biostatistics + ethics. Reported as a three-digit score (mean ~226, passing standard ~198).

questions.promptMd: A 45-year-old with no comorbidities has BP 152/95 on three separate visits. Best initial step?

options.label: B
options.text: Lifestyle modification + lifestyle reassessment in 3-6 months OR start one antihypertensive based on ASCVD risk

questions.explanationMd: Stage 1 HTN: lifestyle changes ± single agent based on risk. ACEi/ARB/CCB/thiazide first-line. β-blockers no longer first-line for uncomplicated HTN.

questions.promptMd: A 50-year-old man should be screened for colon cancer with:

options.label: A
options.text: Colonoscopy at age 50, every 10 years (or alternatives)

questions.explanationMd: USPSTF: colorectal cancer screening starting age 45 (recently lowered). Colonoscopy q10y is the gold-standard. FIT/FOBT yearly + sigmoidoscopy q5y are alternatives.

questions.promptMd: A patient on long-term steroids develops sudden hip pain. Best initial imaging?

options.label: B
options.text: MRI hip (best for early avascular necrosis)

questions.explanationMd: AVN of femoral head: early X-rays often normal. MRI is most sensitive. Causes: steroids, alcoholism, sickle cell, trauma.

questions.promptMd: A 75-year-old on warfarin for AF has GI bleed + INR 4.5. Initial management?

options.label: A
options.text: Hold warfarin + IV vitamin K + 4-factor PCC

questions.explanationMd: Major bleed on warfarin: hold warfarin + IV vit K (5-10 mg) + 4-factor PCC (fastest reversal). FFP if PCC unavailable.

questions.promptMd: An ICU patient with septic shock from pneumonia continues to be hypotensive after 30 mL/kg crystalloid. Next step?

options.label: B
options.text: Start norepinephrine to maintain MAP ≥65 mmHg

options.label: C
options.text: Bolus more fluids regardless of fluid responsiveness

questions.explanationMd: Sepsis bundle: 30 mL/kg crystalloid early. If still hypotensive, NOREPINEPHRINE first-line (highest support, less arrhythmia risk than dopamine). Reassess fluid responsiveness with dynamic measures.

questions.promptMd: A 60-year-old with type 2 DM has persistent HbA1c 8.5 on metformin alone. Best add-on if also has heart failure with reduced EF?
questions.explanationMd: SGLT2i + GLP-1 RA both have cardiovascular + renal benefits in T2DM. SGLT2i specifically reduce HF hospitalizations + slow CKD progression.

questions.promptMd: A 30-year-old has fatigue + weight loss + skin hyperpigmentation + hyponatremia + hyperkalemia + hypotension. Most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanationMd: Addison: ↓cortisol + ↓aldosterone → hypoglycemia, Na loss, K retention, hypotension. ↑ACTH → MSH effect → hyperpigmentation. Diagnosis: AM cortisol + cosyntropin stimulation.

questions.promptMd: A patient is found unresponsive with miosis + respiratory depression + decreased GCS. Initial management?
questions.explanationMd: Opioid OD: triad of altered MS + respiratory depression + miosis. Naloxone (short-acting; may need repeat or drip). Avoid sudden full reversal in chronic users (precipitates withdrawal).

questions.promptMd: A 40-year-old has progressive proximal muscle weakness + heliotrope rash + Gottron papules. Most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanationMd: Dermatomyositis: proximal weakness + heliotrope (purplish eyelid rash) + Gottron (over MCPs). Adults: associated with malignancy — screen.

questions.promptMd: A patient with COPD on home O₂ has worsening dyspnea + ABG showing pH 7.28 / PCO₂ 70 / PO₂ 60 / HCO3 33. Best management?
questions.explanationMd: AECOPD with hypercapnic respiratory failure: BiPAP first-line. Add nebulized bronchodilators, systemic steroids (prednisone 40 mg × 5 days), antibiotics if purulent sputum/severe.

questions.promptMd: A 35-year-old G2P1 at 32 weeks has new-onset HTN 160/110 + proteinuria + headache. Diagnosis + treatment?

options.label: B
options.text: Severe preeclampsia; admit + magnesium sulfate + antihypertensives + plan for delivery

questions.explanationMd: Severe preeclampsia: BP ≥160/110 + proteinuria/end-organ damage. Magnesium for seizure prophylaxis + IV labetalol/hydralazine for BP. Delivery is curative; timing depends on severity + gestational age.

questions.promptMd: A 70-year-old has new-onset right-sided weakness 2 hours after symptom onset. NIHSS 12. CT shows no hemorrhage. Best treatment?

options.label: B
options.text: tPA (within 4.5 hours of last known well, no contraindications) ± mechanical thrombectomy if large vessel occlusion

questions.explanationMd: Acute ischemic stroke within 4.5 h, no contraindications: IV tPA. LVO on imaging: thrombectomy up to 24 h in selected patients. Don't delay — 'time is brain'.

questions.promptMd: Best initial test for suspected pulmonary embolism in a hemodynamically stable patient?

options.label: A
options.text: D-dimer (if low pretest probability) or CT pulmonary angiogram (if high)

questions.explanationMd: Wells score → low pretest: D-dimer (negative rules out). High pretest or positive D-dimer: CTPA. V/Q if CTPA contraindicated (renal failure, contrast allergy, pregnancy).

questions.promptMd: A 60-year-old with ESRD on hemodialysis develops fever + chills + hypotension during dialysis. Most likely cause?
questions.explanationMd: Catheter-related bacteremia is THE most common cause of fever in HD patients with central catheters. Empiric vancomycin + gram-negative coverage; remove catheter for severe sepsis.

questions.promptMd: A 45-year-old has hematochezia + iron-deficiency anemia + family history of colon cancer at age 45. Best initial step?
questions.explanationMd: Iron-deficiency anemia + bleeding + early-onset family history → urgent colonoscopy. Lynch syndrome (HNPCC): MMR genes; screen with IHC/MSI on tumor + germline testing.

questions.promptMd: A test has sensitivity 90%, specificity 80%, prevalence 1% in the population. The positive predictive value (PPV) is approximately:
questions.explanationMd: PPV = TP / (TP + FP). With 1% prevalence: per 10,000 people, 100 have disease (90 TP). 9,900 don't (1,980 FP at 80% spec). PPV ≈ 90/(90+1980) ≈ 4%. Rare diseases → low PPV even with good tests.

questions.promptMd: Number Needed to Treat (NNT) for a drug that reduces death from 10% to 8% over 5 years is:
A study found OR = 2.0 (95% CI 1.5-2.7) for smoking and disease. The result is:

options.label: B
options.text: Statistically significant; smokers have ~2x higher odds

questions.explanationMd: CI does NOT cross 1 (1.5-2.7), so significant at α=0.05. OR=2 means doubled odds. Causation requires more than association.

questions.promptMd: Selection bias most commonly threatens which study type?
questions.explanationMd: Case-control studies are particularly vulnerable to selection bias (how cases + controls are recruited). RCTs minimize selection bias by randomization.

questions.promptMd: A test result with high LR+ (e.g., 10) means:
questions.explanationMd: LR+ > 10 'rules in' (large jump in post-test probability). LR− < 0.1 'rules out'. LR around 1 doesn't help.

questions.promptMd: A trial reports the drug 'lowers cholesterol' (p=0.04) but has 35% loss to follow-up. Most concerning issue?

options.label: B
options.text: Attrition bias may invalidate the result

questions.explanationMd: 35% attrition is severe — those lost to follow-up may differ systematically. Intention-to-treat analysis + sensitivity analyses can partially mitigate; >20% loss is generally a major threat to validity.

questions.promptMd: A type I error (α) is:

options.label: A
options.text: False positive — rejecting a true null hypothesis

options.label: B
options.text: False negative — failing to reject a false null

questions.explanationMd: Type I = α (false positive). Type II = β (false negative). Power = 1 − β. Conventionally α=0.05, β=0.20.
